title: The Great Gatsby — Chapter 1
adaptation_scope: Chapter 1: Nick's framing voice, his move East, dinner at the Buchanans', and his first glimpse of Gatsby.

source_unit_treatments.reason: Establishes narrator and father's advice as framing premise.
Father's quoted advice belongs to the framing beat.
Nick's reflective habit of reserving judgment; thematic texture not a story operation.
Narrator names Gatsby as exception and signals retrospective frame.
Biographical setup: Midwest origin, war, decision to go East.
Nick rents bungalow in West Egg, lives alone with Finnish housekeeper.
Encounter that gives Nick sense of belonging.
Seasonal mood; not a discrete operation.
Establishes West Egg setting and Gatsby's mansion next to Nick's small house.
Sets up Nick's drive to East Egg to dine with the Buchanans; identifies relationships.
Background on Tom's wealth and football past.
Arrival at Buchanan mansion; Tom on porch.
Tom names prior owner and leads Nick inside.
Reveals Daisy and Jordan on couch; Tom shuts windows.
Tom interrupts and asks Nick about work.
Nick's description of Jordan; familiarity foreshadow.
Dinner announced; Tom moves Nick out, cutting off Gatsby topic.
Daisy asks helplessly what to plan.
Daisy accuses Tom of being a brute.
Tom launches into racist 'Rise of the Coloured Empires' tirade.
Phone rings; Tom leaves to take call; tense murmur from Daisy.
Nick asks if something is happening.
Jordan reveals Tom has a mistress in New York.
Second phone call shatters the dinner; subjects vanish.
Post-dinner: Tom and Jordan to library; Nick and Daisy to front porch.
Daisy turbulent; Nick asks about daughter.
Daisy's 'beautiful little fool' monologue—reveals her bitterness about Tom's absence and her daughter.
Inside scene with Jordan reading to Tom.
Daisy reveals Jordan is the golf tournament player.
Daisy jokingly arranges Nick and Jordan.
Silent look between Tom and Daisy.
Nick asks if Jordan's from NY.
Nick says goodbye and is called back.
Nick's private reflection on rumor and reason for going East.
Nick drives away confused; reassesses Tom and Daisy.
Nick returns home; sees Gatsby on lawn.
Gatsby reaches toward green light; vanishes — chapter's iconic closing reveal.

beats.action: Gives Nick advice to reserve judgment because not everyone has had his advantages
beats.result: Nick adopts this advice as a guiding habit
beats.reader_new_info: The narrator is Nick Carraway, speaking retrospectively, shaped by his father's advice.
required_visuals: suggestion of father-son moment from younger years
evidence: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice
just remember that all the people in this world haven't had the advantages that you've had

beats.time: After returning from the East, last autumn
beats.action: Announces that Gatsby alone was exempt from his disillusionment, and that something 'preyed on' Gatsby
beats.result: Reader understands this is Gatsby's story, told in retrospect with foreboding
beats.reader_new_info: Gatsby is the subject; he is gone or finished, and Nick's tale is shaped by what destroyed him.
required_visuals: abstract suggestion of an absent figure (Gatsby unseen)
evidence: Only Gatsby... was exempt from my reaction
what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams
beats.notes: Sets up the retrospective frame; Gatsby is named but unseen.

beats.action: Recounts Midwest origins, Yale graduation, Great War service, and decision to go East to learn the bond business
beats.result: Nick moves East in spring 1922, financed by his father for a year
beats.reader_new_info: Nick is a Midwesterner, Yale grad, war veteran, going East to enter bonds.
required_visuals: Nick in uniform or post-war attire
evidence: I graduated from New Haven in 1915
I decided to go East and learn the bond business
in the spring of twenty-two

beats.action: Settles into a rented weather-beaten bungalow alone after his housemate is transferred to Washington
beats.result: Nick lives alone with a dog (briefly), old Dodge, and a Finnish housekeeper
beats.reader_new_info: Nick's modest domestic situation in the country.
evidence: a weather-beaten cardboard bungalow at eighty a month
an old Dodge and a Finnish woman

beats.action: Stops Nick to ask directions to West Egg village
beats.result: Nick gives directions and feels suddenly like a local, no longer lonely
beats.reader_new_info: Nick begins to feel rooted in his new neighborhood.
evidence: How do you get to West Egg village?
I was a guide, a pathfinder, an original settler

beats.action: Describes West Egg geography and his small house wedged between the colossal mansion of a Mr. Gatsby and another estate
beats.result: Reader knows the spatial relationship: Nick lives next door to Gatsby's mansion at the tip of West Egg
beats.reader_new_info: Nick's neighbor is a Mr. Gatsby whom he does not yet know; the mansion is enormous.
required_visuals: map-like view of two Eggs and bay
Gatsby's huge mansion with tower and pool
Nick's small bungalow squeezed beside it
evidence: I lived at West Egg
It was Gatsby's mansion
as I didn't know Mr. Gatsby

beats.action: Identifies Daisy as his second cousin once removed and Tom as a former college acquaintance and ex-football star, and drives to East Egg to dine with them
beats.result: Nick goes to dinner at the Buchanans'
beats.reader_new_info: Nick is related to Daisy; knew Tom at Yale; Tom is wealthy and brought polo ponies East.
required_visuals: Nick driving across the bay toward East Egg
evidence: I drove over there to have dinner with the Tom Buchanans
Daisy was my second cousin once removed
he'd brought down a string of polo ponies from Lake Forest

beats.scene: Buchanan mansion front porch, East Egg
beats.action: Stands on the porch in riding clothes as Nick arrives at the cheerful Georgian Colonial mansion
beats.result: Nick observes Tom's hardened, powerful, arrogant adult appearance
beats.reader_new_info: Tom is physically imposing, arrogant, and cruel-bodied; the Buchanan estate is grand.
required_visuals: Tom in riding clothes on porch, legs apart
evidence: Tom Buchanan in riding clothes was standing with his legs apart on the front porch
a cruel body
gruff husky tenor

beats.action: Turns Nick around and gestures over the grounds, mentioning the previous owner Demaine, then leads him inside
beats.result: Tom physically directs Nick; displays proprietary pride
beats.reader_new_info: Tom is controlling and proud of his estate.
required_visuals: Tom moving Nick by the arm
evidence: Turning me around by one arm
It belonged to Demaine, the oil man. We'll go inside.

beats.action: Enters a bright rosy room with windblown curtains and French windows open on both ends
beats.result: Reader sees the airy, wind-filled salon as the setting for the introduction of the women
beats.reader_new_info: Interior of Buchanan house is grand, breezy, almost dreamlike.
evidence: bright rosy-coloured space
curtains in at one end and out the other like pale flags

beats.action: Shuts the rear windows, stilling the wind so the two young women in white on the couch settle to view
beats.result: Daisy and an unnamed girl (Jordan) are revealed on the couch
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy and another young woman are introduced; one is a stranger to Nick.
required_visuals: two women in white on enormous couch
evidence: two young women were buoyed up as though upon an anchored balloon
Tom Buchanan shut the rear windows

beats.action: Laughs, holds Nick's hand, says she is 'paralysed with happiness,' and murmurs that the other girl's surname is Baker
beats.result: Daisy and Jordan are introduced; Jordan nods minimally
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy is charming and performative; the other woman is Miss Baker.
evidence: I'm p-paralysed with happiness
the surname of the balancing girl was Baker

beats.action: Asks if people in Chicago miss her, then abruptly mentions her three-year-old daughter Nick has never seen
beats.result: Daisy is briefly delighted by gossip and references her child
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy has a three-year-old daughter; she misses Chicago attention.
required_visuals: Daisy and Nick in animated exchange on couch
evidence: Do they miss me?
She's three years old. Haven't you ever seen her?

beats.action: Interrupts Daisy, asks Nick about his bond work and dismissively claims never to have heard of his firm; Nick retorts; Tom affirms he intends to stay East
beats.result: Brief friction between Nick and Tom established; Tom intends to live East
beats.reader_new_info: Tom is dismissive and territorial; intends to remain in the East.
required_visuals: Tom resting hand on Nick's shoulder
evidence: What you doing, Nick?
Never heard of them
I'd be a God damned fool to live anywhere else

beats.action: Stands up suddenly, complains of stiffness, refuses cocktail because she is 'in training,' prompting Tom's mocking
beats.result: Jordan becomes an active participant; her athletic discipline is suggested
beats.reader_new_info: Jordan is athletic and self-disciplined.
evidence: I'm absolutely in training
How you ever get anything done is beyond me

beats.action: Mentions she knows someone in West Egg and names Gatsby; Daisy reacts with startled 'What Gatsby?'
beats.result: Gatsby's name surfaces aloud and visibly disturbs Daisy
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy has some recognition of, or reaction to, the name Gatsby.
evidence: You must know Gatsby
What Gatsby?

beats.action: Wedges Nick's arm under his and compels him to dinner before Nick can answer about Gatsby
beats.result: Conversation about Gatsby is cut off; the group moves to the porch for dinner
beats.reader_new_info: Tom physically controls and redirects the conversation away from Gatsby.
required_visuals: Tom steering Nick by the arm
group moving to rosy candlelit porch
evidence: Before I could reply that he was my neighbour dinner was announced
compelled me from the room as though he were moving a checker

beats.action: Shows her bruised knuckle and accuses Tom of being a 'brute' and 'hulking' specimen; Tom objects to the word
beats.result: Daisy reveals a physical mark from Tom; Tom reacts crossly
beats.reader_new_info: Tom has hurt Daisy physically, even if 'unintentionally'; their marriage has violence.
evidence: the knuckle was black and blue
You did it, Tom
a great, big, hulking physical specimen

beats.action: Launches into a racist diatribe about 'The Rise of the Coloured Empires' by Goddard, claiming the white/Nordic race must dominate; Daisy mocks him sarcastically
beats.result: Tom's bigotry and pretensions to intellectualism are exposed; Daisy undermines him
beats.reader_new_info: Tom is a racist bully obsessed with white-supremacist pseudoscience; Daisy holds him in light contempt.
forbidden_visuals: the book itself prominently iconized as theme prop beyond table reference
evidence: The Rise of the Coloured Empires by this man Goddard
the white race will be... utterly submerged
We've got to beat them down

beats.action: Leaves the table without a word to take a telephone call inside, prompting a tense murmur from Daisy in the next room
beats.result: The dinner is interrupted; the household tension rises
beats.reader_new_info: A phone call disrupts the dinner; something private is happening.
evidence: the telephone rang inside and the butler left the porch
a subdued impassioned murmur was audible in the room beyond

beats.time: While Tom and Daisy are inside
beats.action: Tells Nick that Tom has a woman in New York who has the indecency to telephone him at dinner
beats.result: Nick learns of Tom's affair
beats.reader_new_info: Tom is having an affair with a woman in New York; she is calling now.
required_visuals: Jordan leaning close to Nick at the table, candlelight
evidence: Tom's got some woman in New York
She might have the decency not to telephone him at dinner time

beats.action: Returns to the table with strained gaiety, deflects with chatter about a nightingale, then plays sentimental with Tom
beats.result: Daisy masks the rupture with performance
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy responds to humiliation by performing romance, not confrontation.
forbidden_visuals: actual nightingale closeup as iconic motif
evidence: It couldn't be helped!
There's a bird on the lawn that I think must be a nightingale

beats.action: The phone rings again; Daisy shakes her head at Tom and the dinner conversation collapses entirely
beats.result: The dinner fractures; everyone is conscious of the fifth, intruding presence
beats.reader_new_info: The mistress's calls dominate the household's evening.
evidence: The telephone rang inside, startlingly
this fifth guest's shrill metallic urgency

beats.action: Follows Daisy to a wicker settee on the front porch where she confesses she has had a bad time and become cynical
beats.result: Nick and Daisy are alone; Daisy begins to disclose her unhappiness
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy has suffered and is bitter; she remarks Nick missed her wedding.
forbidden_visuals: Tom and Jordan in this image
evidence: I followed Daisy around a chain of connecting verandas
I've had a very bad time, Nick, and I'm pretty cynical about everything

beats.action: Tells Nick that when her daughter was born and Tom was absent, she wept and said she hoped the girl would be 'a beautiful little fool,' then declares she is 'sophisticated'
beats.result: Daisy reveals her despair about marriage, motherhood, and being a woman in her world
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy was abandoned by Tom even at her daughter's birth; she is profoundly disillusioned.
forbidden_visuals: hospital scene shown literally beyond gentle indication
evidence: I hope she'll be a fool—that's the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool
I've been everywhere and seen everything

beats.action: Senses Daisy's basic insincerity and feels manipulated
beats.result: Nick distrusts the emotional performance
beats.reader_new_info: Nick perceives Daisy and Tom as colluding in some 'distinguished secret society' of cynicism.
evidence: I felt the basic insincerity of what she had said
an absolute smirk on her lovely face

beats.action: Finishes reading the Saturday Evening Post aloud to Tom, stands, and announces it is time for bed
beats.result: The group is reassembled; Jordan signals the close of the evening
beats.reader_new_info: Jordan and Tom have been quietly together; she sets the evening's end.
required_visuals: Jordan and Tom at couch with magazine
forbidden_visuals: romantic intimacy between Tom and Jordan beyond text
evidence: she read aloud to him from the Saturday Evening Post
Time for this good girl to go to bed

beats.action: Explains Jordan will play in a Westchester tournament, prompting Nick to recognize her as Jordan Baker the golfer and dimly recall an unpleasant story about her
beats.result: Jordan is identified as a public sporting figure; an unspecified scandal looms in Nick's memory
beats.reader_new_info: Jordan is a known professional golfer; there is an unflattering story about her Nick has forgotten.
evidence: Jordan's going to play in the tournament tomorrow
I had heard some story of her too, a critical, unpleasant story

beats.action: Half-jokingly proposes to arrange a romance between Nick and Jordan as Jordan says good night
beats.result: A future pairing is suggested; Jordan exits
beats.reader_new_info: Daisy is matchmaking Nick with Jordan.
forbidden_visuals: actual linen closets / boat as comic literal panels emphasized as plot
evidence: In fact I think I'll arrange a marriage
Good night, Mr. Carraway. See you anon

beats.action: Disparages Jordan's family freedoms and pressures Daisy about her veranda conversation with Nick; Daisy deflects
beats.result: Tom's suspicion and possessiveness about both his wife and household guests is exposed
beats.reader_new_info: Tom is jealous and controlling beyond his affair; Daisy is from Louisville.
evidence: Did you give Nick a little heart to heart talk on the veranda?
Don't believe everything you hear, Nick

beats.action: Calls Nick back as he starts his car to confront him about a rumor that he is engaged out West; Nick denies it
beats.result: Rumor is aired; Nick denies any engagement
beats.reader_new_info: There is a Midwestern engagement rumor about Nick; he denies it.
required_visuals: Tom and Daisy in lit doorway
evidence: We heard you were engaged to a girl out West
It's a libel. I'm too poor

beats.action: Drives off feeling confused and disgusted by Daisy's passivity and Tom's combination of infidelity and pseudo-intellectual bigotry
beats.result: Nick reassesses his cousins critically
beats.reader_new_info: Nick judges that Daisy ought to leave Tom but won't; the Buchanans' moral hollowness is set.
required_visuals: summer roadhouses, petrol pumps with red lights
evidence: the thing for Daisy to do was to rush out of the house, child in arms
he had been depressed by a book

beats.scene: Nick's West Egg yard, beside Gatsby's mansion
beats.action: Returns home, sits on an old grass roller, and spots a man—surmised to be Gatsby—standing on his neighbor's lawn, looking at the stars
beats.result: Gatsby is glimpsed for the first time, alone in the night
beats.reader_new_info: Nick sees his neighbor Gatsby in person for the first time.
required_visuals: distant figure on lawn, hands in pockets, looking up
evidence: a figure had emerged from the shadow of my neighbour's mansion
it was Mr. Gatsby himself

beats.action: Stretches his arms toward the dark water, trembling, reaching toward a single distant green light, then vanishes when Nick looks again
beats.object: The far green light across the water
beats.result: Nick witnesses Gatsby's first iconic gesture: yearning across the bay toward a green light
beats.reader_new_info: Gatsby is fixated on something across the water represented by a far green light, and is emotionally moved by it; he disappears, leaving Nick alone.
required_visuals: Gatsby reaching arms toward dark water
single distant green light at end of dock
Nick looking on, then empty lawn
forbidden_visuals: Gatsby's face turned to camera (he remains far)
evidence: he stretched out his arms toward the dark water
a single green light, minute and far away, that might have been the end of a dock
he had vanished, and I was alone again in the unquiet darkness
beats.notes: Chapter's closing image. Do not over-attach symbolic captions; only what is on the page.
